newsitem.title: POLAND: First firm to start Polish OTC trade December 6.
newsitem.headline: First firm to start Polish OTC trade December 6.

text.p: The first firm approved for trade on Poland's nascent over-the-counter market, machine-tool maker Rafamet SA, will start trade there on December 6, the company's deputy president said on Thursday.

Emanuel Wons told Reuters that the OTC market, to be called Centralna Tabela Ofert (CeTO), had approved Rafamet shares for trade on the condition that they be accepted by the National Securities Depository (KDPW).
"Today all documents were sent to the KDPW...and CetO's decision was qualified because before CeTO we need to send documents to the KDPW," Wons told Reuters.
Earlier this month Rafamet, whose full name is Fabryka Obrabiarek Rafamet SA, became the first firm to have its shares cleared for OTC trade by the Polish Securities Commission (KPW).
All the firm's 1,439,567 shares were approved for trade.
Rafamet made a net profit of 9.6 million zlotys last year on sales of 30.8 millon zlotys and earned 0.1 million zlotys over this year's first three quarters on sales of 25.9 million.
Its main shareholders are Bank Handlowy SA and Bank Slaski, with 38.16 percent each, and the state treasury, with 23.68 percent.
